## Standards

<a id="TypeScriptLibraries"></a>

### TypeScript's libraries of types

`TypeScriptLibraries` · `src/typescript.ts:38`

The declaration files TypeScript ships with its compiler: those of ECMAScript are named lib.es5.d.ts, lib.es2015.core.d.ts and so on; the others declare what a host gives (lib.dom.d.ts, a browser's; lib.webworker.d.ts, a worker's). A global declared only by ECMAScript's does nothing outside, but for a few members (Math.random, Date.now).

Source: TypeScript, the lib option and the declaration files under src/lib of the compiler · `https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#lib`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ecmaScript` | `lib.es` | How the file of an ECMAScript library of types starts its name |

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [A specification that runs](product.md#ExecutableSpecification)
- Used by: [Static reading](engine.md#StaticAnalysis)

<a id="TypeScriptSyntax"></a>

### The syntax of the programs Trame writes

`TypeScriptSyntax` · `src/typescript.ts:256`

ECMAScript's grammar, and the few constructs of TypeScript an assembled program uses (a type assertion, an object type, a union). The marks that several constructs share are here, with the layout of the programs: a space between tokens where it reads better, two spaces before an element on a line of its own.

Source: ECMA-262, ECMAScript 2024 (§ 12 lexical grammar, § 13 expressions, § 14 statements, § 16 modules); TypeScript 5.6 handbook (type assertions, object types, union types) · `https://tc39.es/ecma262/2024/`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `endOfLine` | `"\n"` | Ends each line of a program (refines TextFile.endOfLine) |
| `space` | `" "` | Separates two tokens where the layout wants it (§ 12.2: U+0020) |
| `indent` | `"  "` | Begins an element written on a line of its own: two spaces |
| `comma` | `,` | Separates the elements of a list: arguments, properties, elements of an array (§ 12.8) |
| `openParenthesis` | `(` | Opens arguments, a condition, a group (§ 12.8) |
| `closeParenthesis` | `)` | Closes what ( opened |
| `openBrace` | `{` | Opens an object, the names of an import, an object type (§ 12.8) |
| `closeBrace` | `}` | Closes what { opened |
| `equals` | `=` | Gives a value: the initializer of a declaration, an assignment (§ 12.8) |
| `colon` | `:` | Separates a property's name from its value or its type (§ 12.8) |
| `importKeyword` | `import` | Opens an import declaration (§ 16.2.2) |
| `fromKeyword` | `from` | Introduces the module an import reads (§ 16.2.2) |
| `undefined` | `undefined` | The value of what is not there (§ 19.1.4), and its type |
| `stringType` | `string` | The type of texts (TypeScript) |
| `numberType` | `number` | The type of numbers (TypeScript) |
| `docComment` | `/**` | Opens a documentation comment: a multi-line comment whose first character is an asterisk (JSDoc) |
| `commentEnd` | `*/` | Closes a multi-line comment (§ 12.4) |

## Vocabulary

<a id="WorldGlobals"></a>

### Globals that reach outside

`WorldGlobals` · `src/typescript.ts:53`

The globals through which a body would touch the world: the network, the process, the time, randomness, storage. Only the kinds that may touch the platform (implementations) use them; the TypeScript queries watch each one.

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `fetch` | The network (WHATWG Fetch) |
| `process` | The running process: its arguments, its environment, its exit |
| `require` | Loads a module that no import declares |
| `globalThis` | The global object, and through it everything else |
| `setTimeout` | The time: runs code later |
| `setInterval` | The time: runs code again and again |
| `setImmediate` | The event loop: runs code after the current turn |
| `crypto` | Randomness, and the platform's cryptography |
| `performance` | The time, measured by the platform |
| `XMLHttpRequest` | The network, the older way |
| `WebSocket` | The network, a connection kept open |
| `localStorage` | The browser's storage |
| `Date.now` | The time: the current instant |
| `Math.random` | Randomness |
| `new Date()` | The time: a date made of the current instant |

- Owner: trame
- Globals watched in: [TypeScript](#TypeScript)

## Language

<a id="TypeScript"></a>

### TypeScript

`TypeScript` · `src/typescript.ts:79` · status: **held**

The language of the graph, its kinds and its bodies. Read with the tree-sitter grammar for TypeScript: literals, names, imports, roles, the globals that reach outside, the default export, and the inline bodies of declarations.

Grammar: [Grammar of TypeScript](packages.md#TypeScriptGrammar) `0.23.2` (`tree-sitter-typescript/tree-sitter-typescript.wasm`) · files `.ts` · named `typescript` in bodies

<details><summary>values: The values written in the code: a negative number is the minus and its number</summary>

```scheme
(unary_expression operator: "-" argument: (number)) @literal.number
(number) @literal.number
(string) @literal.text
(template_string) @literal.template
(regex) @literal.regex
```

</details>

<details><summary>parts: What a text is made of: its fragments, its escape sequences, what a template substitutes</summary>

```scheme
(string (string_fragment) @literal.part)
(template_string (string_fragment) @literal.part)
(escape_sequence) @literal.escape
(template_substitution (_) @literal.substitution)
```

</details>

<details><summary>keys: A key written as a text that is not an identifier ("content-type"): a value disguised as a name</summary>

```scheme
((pair key: (string) @literal.key) (#not-match? @literal.key "^[\"'][A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*[\"']$"))
```

</details>

<details><summary>names: What is written like a value but names something: a key, a property read by its name, a re-exported module, the directive, the types</summary>

```scheme
(pair key: (string) @name)
(public_field_definition name: (string) @name)
(method_definition name: (string) @name)
(subscript_expression index: (string) @name)
(export_statement source: (string) @name)
((expression_statement (string) @name) (#eq? @name "\"use strict\""))
(literal_type) @name
(type_annotation) @name
(type_arguments) @name
(type_parameters) @name
(type_query) @name
(interface_declaration) @name
(type_alias_declaration) @name
```

</details>

<details><summary>imports: The modules imported: for their types only, unless a default, a namespace, a name without type, a bare import or a load asks for the value</summary>

```scheme
(import_statement source: (string) @import.type)
((import_statement (import_clause (identifier)) source: (string) @import.value) @_import (#not-match? @_import "^import\\s+type\\s"))
((import_statement (import_clause (namespace_import)) source: (string) @import.value) @_import (#not-match? @_import "^import\\s+type\\s"))
((import_statement (import_clause (named_imports (import_specifier) @_specifier)) source: (string) @import.value) @_import
  (#not-match? @_specifier "^type\\s") (#not-match? @_import "^import\\s+type\\s"))
((import_statement source: (string) @import.value) @_import (#match? @_import "^import\\s*[\"']"))
(call_expression function: (import) arguments: (arguments . (string) @import.value))
((call_expression function: (import) arguments: (arguments . (_) @import.computed)) (#not-match? @import.computed "^[\"']"))
```

</details>

<details><summary>locals: The names a body defines: variables, parameters, functions, what it imports. They hide a global of the same name</summary>

```scheme
(variable_declarator name: (identifier) @local.definition)
(required_parameter pattern: (identifier) @local.definition)
(optional_parameter pattern: (identifier) @local.definition)
(function_declaration name: (identifier) @local.definition)
(catch_clause parameter: (identifier) @local.definition)
(shorthand_property_identifier_pattern) @local.definition
(pair_pattern value: (identifier) @local.definition)
(array_pattern (identifier) @local.definition)
(assignment_pattern left: (identifier) @local.definition)
(import_clause (identifier) @local.definition)
(namespace_import (identifier) @local.definition)
(import_specifier name: (identifier) @local.definition)
(import_specifier alias: (identifier) @local.definition)
```

</details>

<details><summary>globals: The globals that reach outside (WorldGlobals): an identifier, a member read, a date made of the current instant</summary>

```scheme
((identifier) @global (#any-of? @global "fetch" "process" "require" "globalThis" "setTimeout" "setInterval" "setImmediate" "crypto" "performance" "XMLHttpRequest" "WebSocket" "localStorage"))
((shorthand_property_identifier) @global (#any-of? @global "fetch" "process" "require" "globalThis" "setTimeout" "setInterval" "setImmediate" "crypto" "performance" "XMLHttpRequest" "WebSocket" "localStorage"))
((member_expression object: (identifier) @global.name) @global (#any-of? @global "Date.now" "Math.random"))
((new_expression constructor: (identifier) @global.name) @global (#any-of? @global "new Date()"))
```

</details>

<details><summary>entry: What a body gives: its default export</summary>

```scheme
(export_statement "default") @entry
```

</details>

<details><summary>bodies: Where an inline body is: the declarations of a module, and the properties of what they declare</summary>

```scheme
(program (_) @declaration)
(pair key: (property_identifier) @body.name value: (_) @body)
```

</details>

## Function

<a id="TypeScriptWriter"></a>

### TypeScript writer

`TypeScriptWriter` · `src/typescript.ts:775` · status: **held**

Writes the program of an assembled component, always frozen, with the syntax elements above: the build order, the implementation chosen for each port and the values of the graph are written in it; it imports only the bodies, the prelude's tooling and the declarations it must read. What it writes is read back before it is written (Drivers).
